issues: ATAC 0.163 is within 1.7x of the 0.1 cutoff
ATAC replicate GSM7256892 = 0.032 -> gate flips to FAIL
specificity never assessed (null in all 199 rows)
in-sample: Ito thresholds tuned on these same guides
rationale: The gate passed and the guide edited at 91%, but that pass depends entirely on choosing ATAC replicate GSM6896554; under the other replicate in the same supplementary table this guide fails ATAC>=0.1. A correct prediction reached through a coin-flip input is not evidence the metric works.

issues: guide 1 rejected by DeepSpCas9 58.4 vs cutoff 60, yet edited 93%
rationale: Both guides edit efficiently (93%, 85%) and sequence_efficacy ranks them highly, so the ranking signal is sound here. But one was excluded by a 1.6-point DeepSpCas9 shortfall, showing the hard cutoff discards good guides for no biological reason.

issues: guide with CHOPCHOP 0.07 / DeepSpCas9 19.5 still edited 53.5%
rationale: The lower-scoring of the two guides (sequence_efficacy 0.13, bottom of the entire dataset) out-edited the higher-scoring one, 53.5% vs 39.5%. The metric's ordering is inverted at this locus.

Gate passed with ATAC 0.806, eight times the cutoff, so this call is robust to ATAC replicate choice and normalization, and the guide edited at 70%. Confidence is capped by the unassessed specificity term and the single-guide sample.

issues: two guides share ATAC 0.062 but edited 88.75% vs 0.0%
zero-inflated indel (0.0 may be assay failure)
rationale: Both guides have identical accessibility and near-identical sequence_efficacy (0.281 vs 0.268), yet one edits at 88.75% and the other at 0%. This is the cleanest demonstration in the dataset that the score has no resolution at the within-locus level, which is exactly the level at which a user picks a guide.

issues: all three guides highly accessible (ATAC 0.60-0.81) but indel 1.5/70/0
rationale: Open chromatin across all three guides yet outcomes span 0-70%, so the entire discriminative burden falls on the sequence term. The gate call was correct only because CHOPCHOP separated the guides, not because of the cell-context component.

issues: best-editing guide (81%) has the lowest ATAC in the gene (0.0155)
gene name collides with whitespace-padded duplicate 'CDKN2C '
rationale: The guide with 81% indel sits at ATAC 0.0155, roughly one sixth of the cutoff, while the guide at ATAC 0.352 edited at 62% and the one at 0.0387 edited at 0%. Accessibility runs backwards against outcome at this locus.

issues: gene name has trailing whitespace - phantom duplicate of CDKN2C
no gene-name normalization anywhere in the pipeline
rationale: This is not a real gene; it is CDKN2C with a trailing space that survived ingestion untouched, splitting one locus into two records. Any downstream gene-level grouping, provenance link or per-gene aggregation will silently mis-handle it.

issues: sole gate pass had indel 51.5%, within replicate noise of the 50% label boundary
binary >50% ground-truth label is brittle near the cutoff
rationale: The ATAC gate correctly blocked a high-CHOPCHOP guide that only reached 15% indel, which is a genuine save. But the one guide counted as a true positive edited at 51.5%, so its TP status rests on a 1.5-point margin against an arbitrary threshold.

issues: both guides edited ~55% despite bottom-quartile sequence scores
rationale: sequence_efficacy of 0.38 and 0.19 predicted failure, yet both guides edited at 56% and 55.5%. The metric would have discarded two working guides at this locus.

Gate passed with ATAC 1.29, far above the cutoff and therefore robust to replicate and normalization choices, and indel was 57%. Only marginally above the >50% boundary, and a single guide gives no internal replication.
The guide the metric ranks lowest at this locus (sequence_efficacy 0.207) is the one that worked, at 66.5% indel, while the higher-ranked guide gave 0%. Ordering is inverted.

issues: all three guides fail and all three are predicted to fail - concordant but uninformative
DNMT3A is in Ito's prospective validation set, yet none of these guides work
rationale: The metric correctly predicts failure for all three guides (indel 19%, 0%, 0%), which is real concordance. But agreement on an all-negative locus carries much less information than a discriminating call, and none of these are the DNMT3A guides Ito prospectively validated.

issues: guide with CHOPCHOP 0.91 rejected by DeepSpCas9 53.9, edited 75%
second guide rejected by DeepSpCas9 59.1 vs cutoff 60
rationale: The best-editing guide (75%) was rejected despite a near-top CHOPCHOP score of 0.91, and another was rejected by a 0.9-point DeepSpCas9 shortfall. The AND-gate structure means a single component can veto strong evidence from the others.

issues: ATAC gate false negative: 87% indel rejected at ATAC 0.0697
second guide at ATAC 0.697 (10x cutoff) edited only 47.5%
accessibility wrong in both directions at the same locus
rationale: The guide with low accessibility edited at 87% and the guide with ten-fold higher accessibility edited at 47.5%. Accessibility is not merely uninformative here, it is actively misleading in both directions within a single gene.

issues: zero-inflated indel (both guides exactly 0.0, may be assay failure)
rationale: Both guides scored low and both gave 0% indel, so the metric is correct. Exact 0.0 values cannot be distinguished from amplicon or ICE failure, so this concordance may be partly artifactual.

issues: both efficient guides rejected, by two different gate components
ATAC gate false negative: 75% indel rejected at ATAC 0.031
CHOPCHOP gate false negative: 84% indel rejected at CHOPCHOP 0.10
rationale: Both DPH5 guides edited well (84% and 75%) and the rule rejected both, one on accessibility and one on CHOPCHOP. A gene where every working guide is filtered out is a total failure of the selection rule, not a marginal one.

issues: whole locus refractory (max indel 17.5%) - possible unmodeled locus-level confounder
rationale: This is the ATAC term's single best save: a guide with DeepSpCas9 80.7 and CHOPCHOP 0.97, near the top of the dataset, gave 1.0% indel and was correctly blocked by ATAC 0.0232. Confidence is still capped because all five guides underperform, suggesting a locus-level factor the score does not represent.
The lowest DeepSpCas9 guide outperformed the highest one at this locus. Three guides give no consistent ordering.
All three guides fail CHOPCHOP badly (0.04-0.09) yet outcomes range 3-55%, so the score cannot separate them. The best-editing guide is one the metric ranks lowest.

issues: concordant but low-information (four of five guides under 16% indel)
rationale: Five guides all score modestly and mostly fail, which the metric gets right. The one partial exception (40.5% indel) is not resolved by the score, and correctness on an almost-uniformly-negative locus is weak evidence.

issues: ATAC gate false negative: 64.5% indel rejected at ATAC 0.0232
all four guides ATAC 0.0155-0.031, no discrimination
rationale: Accessibility is essentially constant and below cutoff across all four guides while indel spans 2.5-64.5%, so the cell-context term contributes nothing but a blanket veto. It vetoed the second-best guide at the locus.

issues: ATAC 0.523 guide edited 3.5%; ATAC 0.062 guide edited 56%
accessibility anti-correlated with outcome across the locus
rationale: The two most accessible guides (ATAC 0.523 and 0.968) gave the poorest and a middling result, while the least accessible gave 56%. Across four guides accessibility trends the wrong way.

issues: 95.5% indel - highest-editing guide in the gene set - fails all three gate components
rationale: At 95.5% indel this is among the most efficient guides in the entire 199-guide benchmark, and the rule rejects it on DeepSpCas9 (58.4), CHOPCHOP (0.24) and ATAC (0.0232) simultaneously. If the metric cannot recognise the best guide in the dataset, its recall failure is structural rather than incidental.

issues: gate pass at ATAC 0.147 flips to FAIL under replicate GSM7256892 (0.0426)
rationale: The passing guide edited at 84.75% and the two rejected guides gave 0% and 21%, so the ordering is right. The pass itself is replicate-dependent: the second ATAC sample in the same table puts this guide at less than half the cutoff.

issues: gate false positive: passed all three components, indel 36%
DeepSpCas9 78.95 and CHOPCHOP 0.72 both near top of dataset
ATAC 0.132 flips to 0.0213 under replicate GSM7256892
rationale: This guide has near-best-in-dataset sequence scores and passes the accessibility gate, and still underperforms at 36% indel. It is one of only four false positives, and its gate pass would additionally vanish under the alternative ATAC replicate.
Correctly rejected (7% indel), though the rejection came from ATAC 0.0387 while CHOPCHOP was 0.72, so the call hinges on the least reliable component. One guide, one direction, limited evidence.
sequence_efficacy of 0.37 driven by a DeepSpCas9 score of 17.5 predicts near-total failure; the guide edited at 56.5%. This is a direct miss by the component the metric now recommends ranking on.
Low scores across the board and 10.5% indel, so the metric is correct. A single concordant negative is weak evidence for the metric's discriminative value.

issues: gate pass at ATAC 0.116 flips to FAIL under replicate GSM7256892 (0.0853)
rationale: Strong outcome (84% indel) with strong sequence scores (DeepSpCas9 75.9, CHOPCHOP 0.89), so the sequence term alone would have found this guide. The accessibility gate adds nothing here except replicate-dependent fragility.

issues: both guides edited ~80% and both were rejected
one rejected by CHOPCHOP 0.17, one by DeepSpCas9 50.2
double false negative despite ATAC well above cutoff (0.236, 0.201)
rationale: Both guides edit at 82% and 79% with accessibility comfortably above the cutoff, and the sequence components reject both. The metric would return no usable guide for a gene where both tested guides work well.

issues: ATAC 1.75 and 2.39 (17-24x cutoff) yet indel 73.5% and 0%
rationale: Both guides sit deep in open chromatin and the accessibility term saturates at 1.0 for both, yet one edits at 73.5% and the other at 0%. Saturation at ATAC>=0.1 destroys any discrimination the signal might carry at the high end.

issues: ATAC 0.345 guide edited 47.5%, ATAC 0.031 guide edited 42%
rationale: Across five guides spanning ATAC 0.00775-0.345 there is no relationship between accessibility and indel, and the sequence ordering is only loosely correct. The gene's best guide (52.4%) is one the rule rejects.

issues: ATAC gate false negative at 0.0968 vs cutoff 0.1 - guide edited 93.5%
sharpest threshold brittleness case in the dataset (0.3% below cutoff)
rationale: With nine guides this is the best-sampled locus and sequence_efficacy does track outcome reasonably. But the single best guide (93.5% indel) was vetoed by an ATAC value of 0.0968 against a cutoff of 0.1 - a 3-parts-in-1000 miss on a quantized, replicate-unstable measurement, which is not a defensible decision boundary.

issues: all six guides in highly open chromatin (ATAC 0.79-3.4) yet four gave <1% indel
strongest counterexample to the accessibility premise
rationale: KLF2 is maximally accessible across all six guides - ATAC up to 3.4, thirty-four times the cutoff - and four of six guides edit at 0-0.5%. If open chromatin were sufficient for efficient RNP editing, this locus should be uniformly easy; it is not.

Gate passed with ATAC 0.364 (3.6x cutoff, robust to replicate choice), top-decile sequence scores, and 89% indel. This is one of the cleanest supporting cases in the benchmark, limited only by being a single guide and by the universal specificity gap.

issues: both efficient guides rejected by the DeepSpCas9 cutoff
one rejected at DeepSpCas9 58.86 vs cutoff 60 - near-miss
rationale: Both guides edit well (70% and 66%) with accessibility above cutoff, and both are rejected on DeepSpCas9, one by 1.1 points. The rule returns nothing usable for a gene where both tested guides work.

issues: ATAC gate false negative: 74.75% indel rejected at ATAC 0.0658
all four guides ATAC 0.062-0.0852, no discrimination
rationale: Accessibility is nearly constant across all four guides yet indel spans 0-74.75%, so the ATAC term acts only as a uniform veto and removes the one guide that works. The sequence term does correctly rank that guide first.
Predicted to fail and gave 0.5% indel. Correct, but a single negative call provides little evidence about discriminative performance.

issues: gate false positive: passed all three components, indel 5.0%
ATAC gate false negative: 52.5% indel rejected at ATAC 0.0697
gate pass ATAC 0.108 flips to 0.0213 under replicate GSM7256892
PRDM1 is in Ito's prospective validation set yet the rule inverts here
one PRDM1 guide silently dropped in the 205->199 attrition
rationale: The rule's single gate pass at this locus edited at 5% while a guide it rejected edited at 52.5% - the prediction is exactly backwards. That this happens at a gene Ito et al. used for prospective validation makes the in-sample precision figure harder to trust.

issues: guide with the dataset's highest ATAC (6.32) gave 1.0% indel
accessibility maximally wrong at this locus
rationale: The most accessible target region in the entire benchmark (ATAC 6.32, sixty-three times the cutoff) yielded 1% editing. The sequence term correctly predicts failure for all three guides, so the concordance credit belongs entirely to sequence, not cell context.

issues: four ATAC-driven false negatives (87.5%, 86%, 70%, 82.5% indel all rejected)
eight of ten guides edit >60% across ATAC 0.0155-0.116
two guides rejected by DeepSpCas9 near-miss despite 92.5% and 80% indel
rationale: PTEN is the most heavily sampled locus (10 guides) and is the metric's worst failure: the gene edits efficiently almost everywhere while nearly all its targets sit below the ATAC cutoff, producing four accessibility-driven false negatives on guides editing at 70-87.5%. A single accessible locus-wide gate is simply the wrong model for this gene.
CHOPCHOP 0.08 predicted failure and indel was 0.5%. Correct but uninformative as a single negative call.

issues: ATAC gate false negative: 65% indel rejected at ATAC 0.0775
rationale: Both sequence components cleared their thresholds comfortably and the guide edited at 65%, but ATAC 0.0775 vetoed it. The accessibility gate is the sole reason this working guide would not be recommended.

issues: gate pass at ATAC 0.124 flips to FAIL under replicate GSM7256892 (0.032)
rationale: Correct call (67% indel) but the accessibility pass is replicate-dependent, with the alternative ATAC sample placing this target at less than a third of the cutoff. The sequence scores alone would have selected this guide anyway.

issues: zero-inflated indel (both guides exactly 0.0, may be assay failure)
rationale: A genuine ATAC save: a guide with DeepSpCas9 69.9 and CHOPCHOP 0.76 gave 0% indel and was correctly blocked by ATAC 0.0775. The credit is tempered by the fact that both guides read exactly 0.0, which is indistinguishable from assay failure.

issues: ATAC 0.0232 guide edited 70% while ATAC 1.18 guide edited 85.2%
rationale: The gate pass is robust (ATAC 1.18, 85.2% indel) and well supported. But a second guide with poor scores and near-zero accessibility also edited at 70%, so the rule's rejection of it is a false negative that accessibility caused.

issues: guide with DeepSpCas9 53.5 edited 74%; guide with DeepSpCas9 66.8 edited 46%
sequence ordering inverted at this locus
rationale: The higher-scoring guide underperformed the lower-scoring one, 46% versus 74%. Both fail CHOPCHOP so neither would be recommended despite one working well.

issues: both guides rejected; better guide is a false negative
rationale: The ordering is directionally right (higher DeepSpCas9 guide edited better) but both guides fall below CHOPCHOP 0.3, so the rule returns nothing while one guide edits at 53.5%.

The gate pass is correct and well supported (ATAC 0.17, 80.4% indel). The companion guide sits in far more open chromatin (ATAC 1.41) and edits at 0%, correctly rejected by sequence - again showing sequence, not accessibility, is carrying the discrimination.

issues: ATAC gate false negative: 92% indel rejected at ATAC 0.0775
the rejected guide has the highest DeepSpCas9 at the locus (74.0)
rationale: The best guide by both sequence score and measured outcome (92% indel, DeepSpCas9 74.0) was vetoed by accessibility, while a weaker guide (56.5%) passed. The accessibility gate actively inverted the correct selection at this locus.

issues: ATAC replicate GSM7256892 reads 0.0 for all SETDB1 targets vs 0.054-0.124 in GSM6896554
gate pass entirely dependent on replicate choice
best guide (81% indel) rejected by CHOPCHOP 0.20
rationale: The second ATAC replicate reports exactly zero signal at every SETDB1 target while the replicate Agent 4 used reports up to 0.124, so the gate pass here is an artifact of an undocumented sample choice. The locus's best-editing guide (81%) is rejected regardless.

Clean discrimination: the passing guide (ATAC 1.63, CHOPCHOP 0.86) edited at 71% and the rejected guide (CHOPCHOP 0.01) at 0%, with accessibility high for both so sequence did the separating. Robust to ATAC replicate choice, which is why this scores near the top of the range.

issues: gate false positive: passed all three components, indel 29%
rationale: One of the four gate false positives: DeepSpCas9 69.1, CHOPCHOP 0.46, ATAC 0.244 all clear comfortably and the guide reached only 29% indel. A second guide with near-identical scores reached 70.5%, so the metric cannot distinguish them.
Predicted failure (CHOPCHOP 0.10, DeepSpCas9 35.6) and gave 1% indel despite ATAC 0.201 being above cutoff. Correct, and a small point against accessibility being sufficient.

issues: second guide edited 73% but rejected by DeepSpCas9 50.5
rationale: Both guides edit well (67% and 73%) and the metric ranks both near the bottom of the dataset. This locus contributes two clear false negatives driven by the sequence component the pipeline now recommends ranking on.

issues: guide rejected at DeepSpCas9 58.6 vs cutoff 60 edited 66%
rationale: A real ATAC save here: DeepSpCas9 75.6 and CHOPCHOP 0.76 with only 1% indel, correctly blocked by ATAC 0.0232. Offset by a 1.4-point DeepSpCas9 near-miss that discarded a guide editing at 66%.

issues: 28% indel from a guide scored near the dataset minimum - partial discordance
rationale: Predicted failure (CHOPCHOP 0.01, DeepSpCas9 21.4) and gave 28% indel, which is below the 50% label boundary so it counts as correct, but is well above what those scores imply. Directionally right, poorly calibrated.

issues: ATAC gate false negative: 82% indel rejected at ATAC 0.0775
rejected guide had DeepSpCas9 75.1 and CHOPCHOP 0.82
rationale: A guide clearing both sequence thresholds by a wide margin and editing at 82% was vetoed solely by accessibility at 0.0775 against a 0.1 cutoff. The other guide, more accessible at ATAC 0.232, edited at 0%.
Rejected on sequence scores and gave 28% indel, consistent with the prediction. Single-guide evidence only.

issues: ATAC gate false negative: 71.3% indel rejected at ATAC 0.0697
all five guides ATAC 0.0155-0.0697, uniformly below cutoff
rationale: Every TET2 target falls below the ATAC cutoff, so the accessibility gate rejects the whole gene wholesale, including the guide that edits at 71.3%. Sequence_efficacy does correctly rank that guide first at the locus, which is the only reason this is not scored lower.

issues: both guides rejected on CHOPCHOP by 0.02
rationale: Both guides sit at CHOPCHOP 0.28, two hundredths below the 0.3 cutoff, and one edits at 65.5%. The rule discards a working guide on a margin far smaller than the tool's own uncertainty.

issues: 97.4% indel guide rejected at DeepSpCas9 55.5 - largest near-miss false negative in the dataset
second guide at 77.4% indel rejected by CHOPCHOP 0.08
rationale: TNF is the one locus where both ATAC replicates agree (0.155/0.107, 0.279/0.373), so accessibility is trustworthy here - and it is the sequence components that fail, rejecting guides editing at 97.4% and 77.4% while passing one at 59%. The rule selects the worst of the three guides.

issues: ATAC gate false negative: 56.4% indel rejected at ATAC 0.0155
narrow outcome range (19.5-63%) offers little discrimination
rationale: The gate pass (ATAC 0.504, 60.7% indel) is robust, but a guide at ATAC 0.504 with equal accessibility edited at only 19.5%, so accessibility does not separate them. All five guides land in a narrow 19.5-63% band that the score does not resolve.

Mostly concordant across six guides: the gate pass edited at 72% and several low-scoring guides gave near-zero indel, including a good ATAC save (CHOPCHOP 0.73 blocked at ATAC 0.0155, 0% indel). One clear discordance at 56.5% from a bottom-ranked guide.

issues: all ten guides ATAC 0.0155-0.124 - no meaningful discrimination
CHOPCHOP near-miss (0.28) rejected a guide editing at 74.5%
rationale: Ten guides span a narrow accessibility range almost entirely below the cutoff, so the ATAC term functions as a blanket veto and produces three false negatives on guides editing at 59-67%. No TSC1 guide passes the full rule despite four editing above 59%.

issues: gate false positive with 0.0% indel - worst possible outcome for a passing guide
ATAC 0.136 flips to 0.0426 under replicate GSM7256892
zero-inflated indel (0.0 may be assay failure)
rationale: This guide clears all three gate components (DeepSpCas9 67.0, CHOPCHOP 0.49, ATAC 0.136) and produces exactly 0% indel. It is the single most damaging case for the rule's claimed 0.862 precision, and its accessibility pass would not survive the alternative ATAC replicate.

issues: zero-inflated indel (both guides exactly 0.0, may be assay failure)
rationale: Both guides rejected on DeepSpCas9 and both gave 0% indel, so the metric is correct. Two exact zeros again cannot be separated from assay failure.

Both guides correctly rejected (11.5% and 25.5% indel), one by ATAC 0.00775 despite clearing both sequence thresholds - a legitimate accessibility save. Low outcome range limits how much this demonstrates.

issues: narrow outcome range (1.5-39.5%) - no positives to discriminate
rationale: All four guides are correctly predicted to fall below 50%, but none exceeds 39.5%, so this locus tests only the negative direction. The near-minimum-scoring guide still reached 27.5%, indicating poor calibration.

A genuine accessibility save: DeepSpCas9 70.9 and CHOPCHOP 0.60 both pass, and the guide gave only 12% indel, correctly vetoed by ATAC 0.0813. One of the clearer cases where the cell-context term earned its place.

The strongest supporting case in the benchmark: top sequence scores (DeepSpCas9 80.3, CHOPCHOP 0.92), 83% indel, and the only gate-passing guide checked whose ATAC agrees across both replicates (0.147 and 0.160). Still capped by the unassessed specificity term and single-guide sampling.

issues: ATAC replicate GSM7256892 reads exactly 0.0 vs 0.101 in GSM6896554
gate pass sits 0.001 above the cutoff and is fully replicate-dependent
rationale: The guide edits at 73% and passes the rule, but its ATAC value of 0.101 is one thousandth above the cutoff and the second replicate in the same table reports zero signal at this target. The accessibility evidence for this call is effectively noise.

issues: ATAC gate false negative: 72% indel rejected at ATAC 0.0387
rationale: Both sequence thresholds cleared and the guide edited at 72%, but accessibility at 0.0387 vetoed it. Another case where the cell-context term is the sole cause of losing a good guide.

issues: gate pass at ATAC 0.112 flips to FAIL under replicate GSM7256892 (0.032)
rationale: Correct call (58% indel, just above the label boundary) but the accessibility pass has almost no margin and reverses under the alternative ATAC replicate. Sequence scores alone (DeepSpCas9 76.5, CHOPCHOP 0.53) would have selected this guide.
